mechanism: Walk DOM from best Ask/Bid through successive levels, accumulate volume*price until requested size is filled; slippage = VWAP − best price (or −1 if book too thin). Live GetDeviationByVol(vol, MBOOK_ASK|BID) gates entries when implied impact exceeds a threshold.
data_needed: Live MarketBookGet levels (price, volume, side); intended order volume; optional max-slippage threshold.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: MOEX FORTS futures Si-6.15, ED-3.15/ED-6.15, RTS-6.15, RUB/USD, SBRF-6.15; tick/DOM real-time (not bar TF)
why_new_for_mis: Turns the order book into a pre-trade liquidity-impact sensor—MIS can refuse or size-scale trades when expected slippage spikes before any fill.
quote: Knowing the state of the Depth Of Market, we can calculate a potential slippage before conducting a deal.

mechanism: Each bar records open/high/low/close/average of (Ask−Bid)/Point as a separate-window SpreadRecord series. Trading is disabled when current close spread exceeds a green-zone threshold (e.g. >9 pts on Si when typical range was 1–9); EA IsTradeDisable via iCustom CopyBuffer. Spread used as inverse liquidity proxy when DOM history is unavailable.
data_needed: Tick Bid/Ask; bar clock; MaxSpread threshold calibrated to symbol’s typical spread band.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Si-6.15 M1 illustration; EA template any TF; MOEX derivatives
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a cheap bar-path liquidity regime series (spread OHLC+avg) usable as an entry filter without requiring historical DOM.
quote: a spread is inversely correlated with a symbol's liquidity. The narrower the spread, the higher the liquidity, and vice versa.

mechanism: CCanvas dial-gauge library (scale/needle layers, ranges, legends) to visualize profit, spread, margin, ATR, RSI, Force Index. Article is UI rendering and CPU cost of needle fills—not construction of those market sensors.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Dashboard demos of AccountProfit, spread[], ATR/RSI/Force handles on chart
why_new_for_mis: No market sensing idea after full read—dial-gauge chrome and canvas AA only.
quote: The main target of the library creation was the simplicity of adding gauges to an EA or an indicator without delving into the details of drawing and geometry.

mechanism: RSI(8) with 35/65 bands (shifted ±Distans toward 50 after first hit) segments history into overbought/oversold search zones; take High max or Low min in each alternating zone to get four extrema; fit support and resistance as y=kx+b on bar-index x. Channel slope/angle vs time axis labels trend acceleration vs deceleration (regime strength).
data_needed: OHLC + RSI(period≈8); Low_RSI/High_RSI; Distans; bars window; High/Low extrema (wicks included as coded).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: FX pairs; Eric Nyman RSI(8) for non-daily TFs; experimental per-symbol params
why_new_for_mis: Builds dynamic slanted S/R regime geometry from RSI zone extrema rather than fixed horizontal pivots—angle change is an explicit trend-acceleration sensor for MIS.
quote: Increasing the angle of a trend line on a bullish trend implies its acceleration… Trend slowing may suggest its reversal in the nearest future.

mechanism: Map RSI into discrete depth indices: 40–60→0 flat; buy 60–70/70–80/80–90/90–100 → +1..+4; sell symmetric −1..−4. Independently map Bill Williams AC histogram streak length (1–5 rising/falling bars) to speed index ±1..±4. Classify movement as possible/weak/moderate/strong from (index_rsi, index_ac) pairs; flat when RSI index=0.
data_needed: iRSI(period, PRICE_CLOSE); iAC last 5 bars; working TF.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD demos M1–H1; EA optimized on M15; liquid markets assumed
why_new_for_mis: Combines excursion-depth and acceleration-persistence into a compact ordinal regime state usable as a MIS feature beyond raw RSI/AC values.
quote: If we have movement depth indexes and know the movement speed, we can lay down and classify some entry conditions.

mechanism: Exit/reversal when deep trend coexists with opposite AC: buy-close if index_rsi>2 and index_ac<0; sell-close if index_rsi<-2 and index_ac>0 (ball-into-water analogy). Multi-TF stack of same indices filters false H1 reversal when lower TFs still accelerate.
data_needed: Same RSI/AC indices on several TFs (M1/M5/M15/M30/H1 illustrated).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD multi-TF figure; EA single tf input
why_new_for_mis: Explicit depth-vs-acceleration sign divergence as a change/exhaustion sensor, with TF-consistency as a false-signal filter for MIS.
quote: If the price was moving up long enough, its acceleration becomes negative (to the downside). This points to the fact that change in trend is quite possible.

mechanism: Detect bar1 fully inside mother bar2 (high2>high1, low2<low1, body contained); require mother range bar2size>(threshold in points) to reject flat. Place BuyStop above mother High and SellStop below mother Low with interval offset—breakout of the compression range is the change event; both sides armed (two-sided pattern).
data_needed: OHLC of bars 1–2; bar2size threshold; interval; pending expiry.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD D1 example; CADJPY D1 2014 test; significant on H4/D1
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes short-horizon range compression → pending breakout as a MIS change sensor with an explicit non-flat mother-bar gate.
quote: Do not use inside bars repeatedly occurring in the flat market as market entry signals.

mechanism: CMarketBook wraps MarketBookGet with best/last Ask/Bid indexes, Ask/Bid depths, average spread, deferred max Ask/Bid volume and side totals, plus SYMBOL_SESSION_* buy/sell order counts/volumes and open interest. GetDeviationByVol estimates fill impact; panel histograms normalize cell width to max side volume.
data_needed: OnBookEvent subscription; MarketBookGet; SymbolInfoInteger/Double session order and interest fields (MOEX).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Si-9.15, ED-9.15, OFZ2-9.15, GAZP/SBRF futures; DOM event-driven
why_new_for_mis: Packages live book geometry, imbalance, impact, and exchange-wide resting liquidity/OI into one sensing API MIS can poll as a liquidity feature vector.
quote: Often Depth of Market is used by traders to determine the current market liquidity, i.e. Depth of Market is used as an additional instrument to control risks.

mechanism: VR = current tick_volume / mean tick_volume over period_VR. Spindle width ∝ VR/VR_max (scaled by correct_VR and chart pixel scales)—high VR = elevated activity vs recent mean; low VR = quiet. Paired with VWMA = Σ(price·V)/ΣV over period_VWMA as volume-weighted mid of the spindle.
data_needed: tick_volume series; period_VR; period_VWMA; price type for VWMA (O/H/L/C/mid).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 EA test 2013–2015; generic MT5 charts; tick volume
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a normalized per-bar activity sensor (volume vs its own mean) encoded in spindle width—orthogonal to OHLC range alone.
quote: Volume Ratio is equal to the current volume divided by the arithmetic mean of the volumes of the selected period.

mechanism: Classify each spindle by color (up/down), body/shadow ratio terciles (≤1/3, ≤2/3, ≤1), VWMA vs High/Low (above/below/inside), and when inside, Open/Close vs VWMA—30 discrete morphologies. Arrowhead orientation = continuation bias; rhombus (Doji-like) = reversal hint. EA maps each pattern to buy/sell/close/flat.
data_needed: SPC buffers: high/low histogram, open, close, VWMA; body/shadow ratios; pattern action table.
why_new_for_mis: Volume-aware candle morphology state machine (30 classes) is a richer short-horizon regime codebook than classic OHLC candlestick labels.
quote: buy when the arrowhead points up and sell when it points down. Rhombus is a kind of Doji, it indicates a reversal.

mechanism: Collect fractal extrema (min-max-min or max-min-max sets; optional X-bars Fractals with BarsBeside) into CFractalSet; draw equidistant channel via CChartObjectChannel. Sync lines to common start bar preserving slope/width; filter adjacent fractals by BarsBetween and relevant extremum choice. Channel bounds define the local price regime corridor.
data_needed: Fractal indicator (standard or X-bars); BarsBeside, BarsBetween, PrevFracNum; symbol OHLC.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H4 examples; ChannelsPlotter EA; any TF with enough fractals
why_new_for_mis: Auto-updating fractal equidistant corridor is a geometric regime envelope MIS can use as dynamic support/resistance state.
quote: we will attempt to enlighten a dynamic way of building equidistant channels, frequently named as moving channels.

mechanism: On new channel, price_speed_pnt = Normalize(upper[1]−upper[0]); if |speed| > TypeTolerance → ASCENDING or DESCENDING else FLAT. LongCondition only if not descending; ShortCondition only if not ascending; flat allows both border touches.
data_needed: EquidistantChannels upper/lower buffers; TypeTolerance in points.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 2013–2015 tester; fixed channel params from base_signal.set
why_new_for_mis: Classifies the moving channel into asc/desc/flat regime and gates side-of-touch trades—explicit trend-vs-range state from channel geometry.
quote: it is better to sell in a descending channel, and to buy in ascending. If the channel is flat (not inclined), then it is possible to trade based on both borders.

mechanism: Approx width = (upper−lower)/(1+pr_speed). If width ≤ NarrowPips → NARROW: trade breakout beyond outer buffer zone. If width ≥ BroadPips → BROAD: trade rebound into inner/outer border buffer. Mid width → no trade (or later versions still rebound). Separate pattern weights for rebound vs breakout; optional close on NewChannel.
data_needed: Channel borders; NarrowPips/BroadPips; PointsInside/Outside buffers; new-channel flag buffer.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; Every tick based on real ticks; 2013–2015
why_new_for_mis: Channel-width regime switches the sensing mode between compression-breakout and mean-reversion—MIS can treat width as a meta-feature selecting change vs fade models.
quote: If the channel turned out narrow, then when its border is broken, it would be possible to trade towards the breakout direction… If the channel turned out wide, it is possible to trade based on its borders.

mechanism: BUOVB/BEOVB: bar1 High>bar2 High and Low<bar2 Low with opposite body colors and close beyond prior open; require outside-bar range bar1size>threshold to skip flat. Directional pending: BuyStop above outside High (BUOVB) or SellStop below outside Low (BEOVB) with SL beyond opposite extreme—range expansion breakout is the change signal.
data_needed: OHLC bars 1–2; bar1size threshold; interval; TP; expiry.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURAUD and major FX D1 2014; pattern significant on H4/D1
why_new_for_mis: Outside-bar engulfing with minimum range gate is a volatility-expansion change sensor MIS can use as a directional breakout event.
quote: Patterns repeated in flat trading should not be used as a signal for entering the market.
